title: Measurement Data Cleaning Decision Simulator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Decision activity in which learners judge eight anomalies in a synthetic batch of 40 device offset-voltage measurements and commit one of four actions: keep, exclude with log, correct and log, or remeasure. Each anomaly comes with a lab notebook excerpt; one attempt per anomaly in a fixed order, after which the sim reveals the correct action, the reason, and the cleaning log entry. The run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 7 of 8, and a summary of how many rows were kept, excluded, corrected, and sent for remeasurement.

learningObjectives: Judge, for each of eight anomalies in a batch of measurements, whether to keep, exclude with a log, correct and log, or remeasure, with at least 7 of 8 correct
prerequisites: The three rules of honest cleaning: cleaning is a script, every change is logged, remove only for a documented cause
The four responses to an anomaly: keep, exclude with log, correct and log, remeasure

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML buttons reachable with the Tab key and expose aria-pressed for the current choice; the chosen action is shown by a thick border and bold text as well as color; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or X symbols as well as a blue/brown color pair; all text is 16 px or larger.

controls.label: Keep / Exclude with log / Correct and log / Remeasure
controls.purpose: Chooses one of the four actions for the current anomaly. The choice can be changed until Submit; after Submit the buttons are disabled and marked with a check mark (correct action) or an X (wrong pick).

controls.label: Submit / Next Anomaly / See Score
controls.purpose: Submit commits the chosen action (one attempt) and is enabled only after a choice. It then becomes Next Anomaly, and after the eighth anomaly See Score, which shows the score, the mastery statement, and the row summary.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Case-based judgment against a stated criterion (the documented cause) with one attempt per case and an explanatory reveal
keyQuestions: What should happen to this data?
Is there a documented cause for this anomaly?
Can cleaning recover this measurement, or must it be remeasured?
What would be recorded in the cleaning log?
commonMisconceptions: An outlier should be removed because it is an outlier
A suspicious value can be edited in the raw file
Any problem with the data can be fixed by cleaning
assessmentOpportunities: At least 7 of 8 actions matching the answer key on the first attempt is evidence of mastery
Reading the lab notebook excerpt is exploration and is not evidence
